summary: The milestone recorded 2 completed experiments in 0.3 minutes, with 1 compute-bound experiment. The compute entry is at the timing floor, while the protected compute-task GPU-idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction placed the compute-bound experiment at 0.0 minutes, so no data available this milestone identifies which execution phase consumed its time.
The point-in-time GPU state is not joined to experiment phase boundaries, leaving task-scoped accelerator attribution unavailable.
No data available this milestone records whether 2 or more models were loaded in parallel or which runner handled them.
improvements_suggested: Add automatic batches of 8-16 questions per forward pass to the single-process inference path and measure the realized throughput change.
Write monotonic queue, load, inference, verification, and artifact-write timestamps into each experiment receipt.
Attach experiment identity and start/end boundaries to GPU utilization samples.
Record loaded-model count and parallel-versus-sequential mode, selecting DualGPURunner only when 2 or more models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Introduce configurable 8-16 question batching for inference.
Replace disk-mtime-only diagnosis with task-owned monotonic phase receipts.
Persist task-window GPU samples, loaded-model concurrency, and runner selection together.
meta_reflection: The evidence excludes a locked compute-idle finding but cannot explain the compute task's phase costs or establish a missed parallel-model runner dispatch. Batching is the clearest measured tooling hypothesis; milestone-wide savings remain unquantified, so the estimate stays at 0%.
